answer: Divergent-horizon commitment: each agent posts a unique, time-locked prediction (a "comet" hash) about its own future actions over a long horizon, salted per epoch and revealed later. Clones share one code path, so they must commit identically; a single divergent commitment (an "oasis" of unique behavior) exposes the clone cluster. Attacker cost: maintaining N clones requires N distinct forward predictions, forcing genuine branching logic and per-clone state/secrets — breaking the clone property itself.
